title: Practical A/B Framework: Adaptive Sample Sizing, Exposure Throttles, and Auto-Revert Playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and deliver a production-ready A/B testing framework for model versions that combines adaptive sample-size calculation, exposure throttles (time- and traffic-based), automated statistical checks, and deterministic auto-rollback behavior. The goal is to enable product and platform teams to run principled model comparisons with clear safety gates and low operational overhead.
background: Current rollout tooling supports ad-hoc canaries and manual A/B splits but lacks: (1) a standardized experiment spec that encodes hypothesis + primary metric, (2) automated sample-size adaption when variance or event rates differ, (3) traffic throttles that respect latency SLOs and capacity budgets, and (4) a deterministic auto-revert mechanism tied to statistical checks. Multiple incidents showed slow detection of regressions when traffic rates were low or metrics were noisy.
goals: Provide an experiment spec template (hypothesis, primary/secondary metrics, min detectable effect, alpha, power)
Implement adaptive sample-size estimation and runtime re-calibration based on observed variance
Add exposure controls: percent-of-traffic ramps, time-window caps, and request-rate ceilings per cohort
Automate statistical checks (frequentist + optional bayesian) and define deterministic auto-rollback conditions
Expose experiment status and per-metric confidence in Console; ship alerts for early-warning signals
non_goals: Building a full statistical modeling studio — we provide guardrails and defaults, not a custom analytics engine
Support arbitrary offline metric pipelines in v1 — rely on Console metrics and dataplane counters
Replacing canary-based kernel/serving rollout logic — integrations only
success_metrics: Time-to-detection for a 5% degradation on primary metric reduced from median 48h to <8h
Number of manual aborts during rollouts reduced by 60% within two sprints of launch
>70% of internal model experiments created with the new spec within quarter after launch
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Specification and offline simulator + PRD (2 weeks). Phase 2: Implement sample-size engine and exposure throttles in control plane (4 weeks). Phase 3: Integrate statistical check runner and auto-rollback extension (3 weeks). Phase 4: Pilot with two internal product teams (2 weeks). Phase 5: Cross-team rollout and console UX polish (2 weeks).
statistical_tests: Defaults: two-sided t-test for continuous primary metrics, chi-squared for binary metrics, with alpha=0.05 and power=0.8. Implement sequential testing safe-guards (alpha spending / group sequential boundaries) to allow interim looks. Offer a bayesian posterior-check option for teams that prefer probability-of-being-better thresholds. All tests produce effect size, p-value, confidence interval, and required sample remaining when underpowered.
exposure_controls: Traffic split primitives (absolute percentage, cohort-based targeting), adaptive ramp scheduler (initial holdout -> 1% -> geometric ramp with max slope), rate ceilings (requests/min per variant), time-window caps (max exposure minutes per hour), and capacity-aware throttling (integrates with Dedicated capacity telemetry). Defaults prioritize safety: no automatic ramp above 10% until min sample is observed.
safety_gates: Hard Abort: primary metric drops by X sigma within a single analysis window
Soft Hold: variance > threshold or underpowered — pause traffic ramp until metric stability is observed
Circuit Breaker: latency P95 exceeds SLO for variant more than twice baseline for 5 consecutive minutes
Budget Guard: stop further exposure if cumulative token cost for experiment exceeds allocated budget
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit experiment-state events (started, ramp, hold, abort, complete) and per-metric analysis summaries to Console. Create alert rules: critical (auto-rollback triggered), warning (soft hold), and info (near-threshold). Instrumentation includes cohort-level counts, conversions, sample variance, estimated power, and latency distributions. Dashboards prebuilt for experiment owners.
tasks: Finalize experiment spec schema and JSON schema for API
Implement sample-size calculator service with APIs for runtime re-eval
Add exposure scheduler in control plane; integrate rate ceilings with serving runtime
Implement statistical runner + sequential test library; wire to auto-revert hooks
Console: experiment creation UI, status timeline, and metric panels
Documentation and runbook: experiment design checklist and troubleshooting
Pilot run with Search team and Embed product; gather feedback
notes_and_decisions: Decision: use frequentist defaults + optional bayesian path — gives broad familiarity for PMs and DSs
Decision: enforce min-sample before ramps >10% to avoid premature conclusions
Trade-off: sequential testing increases detection speed but complicates error-rate accounting; solution is alpha spending with conservative boundaries
Implementation note: sample-size re-estimation runs every 30 minutes during an experiment
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy metrics lead to false aborts — Mitigation: require consistency across multiple windows and use hold state before abort
Risk: teams misconfigure hypotheses — Mitigation: provide templates and required fields in spec with validation
Risk: interaction with Dedicated autoscaling — Mitigation: integrate capacity signals into exposure scheduler to avoid cost spikes
open_questions: Q: Should we support cohort-level stratified randomization in v1? (trade-off: complexity vs. statistical fidelity)
Q: What are default min-detectable-effect values per metric type? Need DS guidance
Q: How do we surface post-rollback investigation artifacts automatically?
